subtitle: Lesson 19 · Governance, Compliance & Audit

code:
sys_audit entry:
  field       -> which field changed
  old value   -> what it was
  new value   -> what it became
  changed by  -> who
  changed at  -> when

The durable, queryable change-history ledger.
caption: The same kind of trail Lesson 18 argued elevation events need.

eyebrow: The assumption most people get wrong
code:
Common assumption:                   Reality:
"sys_audit exists, so every field    Auditing is configured PER TABLE
 change everywhere must already       and PER FIELD, via the Dictionary
 be tracked."                        entry's Audit setting.

An un-audited field's changes are never
written to sys_audit -- not recoverable later.
caption: The table existing does not mean everything is captured in it.

code:
Field with auditing OFF:
  changes freely, over and over
  -- no sys_audit entry ever created

Querying sys_audit after the fact cannot
recover history that was never captured.
caption: Turning auditing on later does not retroactively fill the gap.

code:
Audit-everything approach:            Selective-audit approach:
- Every field, every table audited    - Sensitive / compliance-relevant
- Large, fast-growing sys_audit          fields audited deliberately
- Real storage + write overhead       - Smaller, actually reviewable
- Mostly never reviewed                  history
caption: Auditing has a real storage and performance cost, not a free safety net.
